summary: NBC News traces how The Epoch Times, launched by Falun Gong practitioners as a free anti-Chinese Communist Party newsletter, became one of America's most influential conservative outlets. Through aggressive pro-Trump advertising, election and Covid misinformation, mass free-copy distribution and big conservative donors, its revenue grew 685% in two years to $122 million in 2021. The paper denies ties to Falun Gong despite shared executives, grants and a media network that leader Li Hongzhi calls "our media."
one_line: NBC News examines how the Falun Gong-run Epoch Times used pro-Trump ads, conspiracy content and donor money to grow into a $122 million conservative media powerhouse.
key_facts: The Epoch Times grew its revenue by 685% in two years, to $122 million in 2021, according to its most recent tax records.
The Epoch Times claims to be the country's fourth-largest newspaper by subscriber count, but it isn't audited by the two major independent collectors of circulation data.
Falun Gong was started by Li Hongzhi in China in 1992; China banned it in 1999 and labeled it a cult after thousands of followers silently protested in Beijing.
The Epoch Times was started in Georgia in 2000 by John Tang, a Falun Gong practitioner who remains its CEO, as a Chinese-language public relations newsletter.
In 2009 Li Hongzhi told Epoch Times volunteers to "Ensure that the paper gains a foothold in ordinary society and turns profitable."
In 2019, following NBC News reporting, Facebook found The Epoch Times had "leveraged foreign actors posing as Americans to push political content" and banned it from advertising.
The Epoch Times mailed 280,000 free copies in Philadelphia alone in 2020 and reported $76 million in subscription revenue in 2021, up from nearly $7 million in 2019.
A former employee said the paper bought data-broker address lists targeting conservatives aged 60 and over to pick likely subscribers.
The Election Integrity Partnership cited The Epoch Times as a "repeat spreader" of false voter fraud stories and a promoter of debunked Dominion and "Stop the Steal" conspiracy theories.
The Epoch Times reported $8.4 million in contributions and grants in 2020 and 2021, including $55,750 from the National Christian Charitable Foundation and $31,000 from Donors Trust in 2021.
In the first half of 2023, The Epoch Times spent 65% more on ads than in the first six months of 2022, with about half its budget going to X, formerly Twitter.
The Epoch Times paid Data Managing Corporation $2.7 million for advertising in 2021; the company's listed address is a New Jersey single-family home owned by an Epoch Times reporter.
In 2021 The Epoch Times gave about $30 million in grants to affiliates, including $10.4 million to Shen Yun and $8.3 million to New Tang Dynasty.
The Epoch Times, New Tang Dynasty and Shen Yun together made up a nearly quarter-billion dollar industry in 2021.
